title: Angle Turns
goal: I can measure angles and find missing angles. I can find the angle between clock hands and turn on the 8-point compass.

learn.intro: You need a 180° protractor and a ruler for this unit. A full turn is 360°, a half turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°. To measure, count up from the 0 on one arm.

example.problem: How big is the angle? Use the scale that starts at 0 on the arm.
steps: Put the centre of the protractor on the corner. Put the 0 line on one arm.
Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm.

example2.problem: What is the angle between the clock hands at 4 o'clock?
steps: A clock has 12 equal spaces in 360°. 360 ÷ 12 = 30, so 1 space is 30°.
At 4 o'clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30°.

howto.title: How to measure
steps: Estimate first. Is it less than 90° or more?
Centre on the corner. 0 line on one arm.
Read from the 0 on that arm. Check with your estimate.

facts.title: Good to know
lines: ∠AOC is the angle at O between OA and OC.

try.text: Ali faces NE. He turns 135° clockwise. Which way does he face now? {circ:E|SE|S|SW}
try.explanation: 135° is 3 steps of 45°. Clockwise from NE: E, SE, S. He faces S.

items.text: Estimate each angle. Then measure it with your protractor. Use a ruler to make the arms longer first.
items.explanation: Each angle starts at 0 on the horizontal arm. a = 25°, b = 65° and c = 130°. Answers within 2° are fine. Angle c is greater than a right angle, so a good estimate is more than 90°.

items.text: Read the angle from the protractor.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Is it smaller or greater than a right angle? {circ:smaller|greater}

items.explanation: Read the scale that starts at 0 on the arm along the baseline: 52°. It is smaller than a right angle. The other scale says 128°, measured from the other arm.

items.text: Rays OA, OB, OC and OD leave O. The 3 small angles lie side by side. Find the angles.

parts.label: d
parts.text: How many angles are there in all? {b}

items.explanation: The angles add. ∠AOC = 25° + 35° = 60°. ∠BOD = 35° + 40° = 75°. ∠AOD = 25° + 35° + 40° = 100°. The angles are AOB, BOC, COD, AOC, BOD and AOD: 6 angles.

items.text: Each step round the compass is 45°. Find the direction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ali faces W. He turns 90° clockwise. He now faces {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Mei faces SE. She turns 180°. She now faces {b}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Siti faces NE. She turns 270° clockwise. She now faces {b}

parts.label: d
parts.text: Ravi turns 135° anticlockwise and now faces S. At first he faced {b}

items.explanation: (a) 90° is 2 steps: W, NW, N. (b) 180° is 4 steps: SE, S, SW, W, NW. (c) 270° is 6 steps: NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW. (d) 135° is 3 steps clockwise from S: SW, W, NW.

items.text: Find the smaller angle between the clock hands.
items.explanation: Each space between numbers is 30°. At 5 o'clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 150°. At 8 o'clock they are 4 spaces apart the short way: 120°. At 11 o'clock they are 1 space apart: 30°.

items.text: Ben faces W. He wants to face NE. What is his smallest turn?
items.explanation: Clockwise from W: NW, N, NE is 3 steps, 135°. Anticlockwise from W: SW, S, SE, E, NE is 5 steps, 225°. The smallest turn is 135° clockwise.

items.text: Each rectangle corner is 90°. Lines split the corners. Find the angles a and b. The drawings are not to scale.
A robot faces E. It turns 135° anticlockwise. Then it turns 90° clockwise. Then it turns 45° clockwise.
items.explanation: 135° anticlockwise from E: NE, N, NW. 90° clockwise from NW: N, NE. 45° clockwise from NE: E. It faces E. The turns add to 135° + 90° + 45° = 270°.

items.text: A corner of a rectangle is split into 2 angles. One angle is 5 times the other.
items.explanation: The corner is 90° and is made of 1 + 5 = 6 equal parts. 90° ÷ 6 = 15° for 1 part. The greater angle is 5 × 15° = 75°.

items.text: How long does the minute hand take to turn through each angle?
items.explanation: The minute hand turns 6° each minute. 90° ÷ 6 = 15. 180° ÷ 6 = 30. 270° ÷ 6 = 45. 60° ÷ 6 = 10.

items.beyond: Angles on a line and at a point
items.text: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Angles around a point add up to 360°.

parts.label: a
parts.text: On a straight line the angles are 47°, 85° and a. a = {b}°

parts.label: b
parts.text: Around a point the angles are 95°, 120°, 78° and b. b = {b}°

items.hint: Add the angles you know. Then take the sum away from the total.

items.text: Find the smaller angle between the clock hands.
items.hint: At half past, the hour hand is halfway between 2 numbers.
items.explanation: At 7:30 the minute hand is on the 6 and the hour hand is halfway between 7 and 8, 1 and a half spaces away: 45°. At 1:30 the hour hand is 4 and a half spaces from the 6: 4 × 30° + 15° = 135°.

items.text: A robot faces N. It turns 90° clockwise, then 135° anticlockwise, then 225° clockwise, then 45° anticlockwise.
items.hint: Count the steps of 45°. Clockwise is plus, anticlockwise is minus.
items.explanation: In steps of 45°: +2, −3, +5, −1. From N: 2 steps is E, then 3 steps back is NW, then 5 steps forward is S, then 1 step back is SE. The turns add to 90° + 135° + 225° + 45° = 495°.

items.text: Four rays leave a point O on a straight line. They make 4 angles. Each angle is 10° greater than the one before it.
items.hint: The 4 angles add up to 180°. Take away the extra degrees first.
items.explanation: The extras are 0, 10, 20 and 30, which make 60°. 180° − 60° = 120°, shared by 4 equal angles: 30°. The greatest is 30° + 30° = 60°.

items.text: A Ferris wheel has 12 equal seats, numbered 1 to 12 clockwise. Seat 1 is at the top.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The seat at the bottom is Seat {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: The smaller angle at the centre between Seat 2 and Seat 9: {b}°

parts.label: c
parts.text: The wheel turns 270° clockwise. Seat 1 is now where Seat {b} was

items.hint: 12 seats share 360°. What is the angle between neighbours?
items.explanation: (a) Seat 1 is opposite Seat 7. (b) Seats 2 to 9 are 7 steps of 30°, which is 210°. The smaller way is 360° − 210° = 150°. (c) 270° ÷ 30° = 9 steps, and 1 + 9 = Seat 10.

items.text: A round pizza is cut from the centre into 4 slices. The 2nd slice is 2 times the 1st. The 3rd and 4th slices are each 3 times the 1st.
items.hint: Count the equal parts: 1 + 2 + 3 + 3. All round is 360°.
items.explanation: The slices are 1, 2, 3 and 3 parts. 9 parts = 360°, so 1 part = 40°. The smallest is 40° and the 4th is 3 × 40° = 120°.

items.text: Think about the smaller angle between the clock hands at each o'clock time. Which times give an angle between 100° and 160°?
items.hint: Write the angle for every o'clock time first.

items.text: Find the smaller angle between the clock hands at 7 o'clock. {b}°
items.explanation: At 7 o'clock the hands are 5 spaces apart the short way. 5 × 30° = 150°.

items.text: Aisha faces S and turns 135° clockwise. Which way does she face now? {b}
items.explanation: 135° is 3 steps of 45°. Clockwise from S: SW, W, NW.

items.text: A corner of a square is split into 2 angles. One angle is 41°. How big is the other? {b}°
items.explanation: The corner is 90°. 90° − 41° = 49°.

items.text: The minute hand moves from 5:10 to 5:35. How many degrees does it turn? {b}°
items.explanation: From 5:10 to 5:35 is 25 minutes. 25 × 6° = 150°.
